input.rationale: Next increment on the open gap: the sweep's configuration events now also exercise joint consensus. Half of the ConfChangeV2 proposals on node 4 carry Transition=ConfChangeTransitionJointImplicit, so the cluster enters a joint configuration (Voters[0] receives the change while Voters[1] keeps the outgoing voters) and, because the implicit transition sets AutoLeave, the leader itself proposes the zero-change leave once the change is applied - the repository's own auto-leave producer rather than a hand-built one. That means decision formation under a joint quorum (a majority in both halves) is now inside the event set, which the previous interpretation's counterevidence named as missing. Draft-side this revision reports invariant_sweep_summary with seeds=60, steps_per_seed=60, elections=468, ordinary proposals=460, conf_change_proposals=356 and violations=0, so still no witness with joint transitions present; that is construction feedback only, so the experiment below requests isolated execution of these bytes. Restarts from persisted storage and the guard's liveness witness remain outside the event set, so the gap stays open.

scope.description: Sixth revision of the same fixed harness; probes A, B and C are unchanged. The sweep keeps four real state machines (ids 1..4, stored ConfState voters {1,2,3}, node 4 registered directly with the network so it starts outside the configuration) and now proposes joint transitions: each configuration event builds a single-change ConfChangeV2 for node 4 (AddLearnerNode, AddNode or RemoveNode) and, with probability 1/2, sets Transition=ConfChangeTransitionJointImplicit, which enters a joint configuration and leaves AutoLeave set so the leader proposes the leaving change itself once the entry is applied. Committed conf changes are still applied through applyConfChange on every node including 4, and the four invariants (at most one leader per term, committed (index,term) consistency, committed-index monotonicity, applied<=committed) are still checked after every event, with invariant_sweep_summary reporting seeds, steps, elections, ordinary proposals, conf_change_proposals and violations. Node restarts and the campaign guard's liveness witness remain outside this revision.
assumptions: Everything comes from the snapshot's own facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, withPeers, newNetwork, nextEnts, confChangeToMsg, applyConfChange, and the AutoLeave path in appliedTo); no production logic is modified.

JointImplicit with a single change is a legitimate way to enter a joint configuration in this library, and the leave-joint proposal is produced by the target's own auto-leave code rather than by the harness.
The operations proposed for node 4 remain safe to apply repeatedly and the configuration cannot be driven into an invalid transition by the random sequence.
Randomness is fixed per seed; absence of violations is a holds-only result for this event set, not a safety proof.

experiment.prefix: For each of 60 seeds: build nodes 1..4 with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); nt := newNetwork(nodes[1],nodes[2],nodes[3]) then nt.peers[4] = nodes[4]. For 60 steps pick one of MsgHup on a random node, MsgProp with a tagged payload, tick() on a random node, isolate a random node, recover, TransferLeader from a random voter to the current leader, a ConfChangeV2 proposal on the leader (single change on node 4, half the time with Transition=JointImplicit), or persist/apply of all nodes; after each step persist/apply nodes 1..4 (applying committed conf changes through applyConfChange) and evaluate the four invariants, emitting a violation event with seed, step, nodes and operands when one is found, and finally emitting invariant_sweep_summary.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and sweep case as the previous execution, with joint transitions added: half of the configuration proposals now use ConfChangeTransitionJointImplicit and therefore enter and (via the target's AutoLeave) leave joint configurations, and only the harness bytes changed to do so. Fresh execution is requested because the harness bytes and the event set changed.

scope.description: One fixed harness with two sourced probes. Probe A (TestAssuranceCampaignWithUnappliedConfChange) covers the campaign admission guard: a voter built from MemoryStorage with entries [1]=normal and [2]=EntryConfChangeV2 at term 1, HardState.Commit=2 and Config.Applied=1, driven by MsgHup and by MsgTimeoutNow (term-carrying), then re-driven after raftLog.appliedTo(2,0); a control node has the same applied/committed gap but a normal entry at index 2. Probe B (TestAssuranceReadIndexAcrossTermChange) covers ReadOnlySafe completion across an authority change: elect a leader over a real 3-node in-process network, commit an entry in its term, admit a MsgReadIndex with no heartbeat responses delivered, then deliver a real higher-term campaign message from peer 2, and finally confirm a read admitted on the new leader with a single peer heartbeat response echoing the leader's context. Each case prints one CA_EVENT JSON line with the observed operands (state, term, vote, applied, committed, has_unapplied, unconfirmed_reads, confirmed_reads, read_states, vote targets, read index).
assumptions: Both probes use the snapshot's own test facilities (newTestRaft/newTestConfig/newTestMemoryStorage/withPeers/newNetwork) in one process.
Probe A's supplied state is a real MemoryStorage prefix plus a HardState and Config.Applied=1, so the applied<committed gap is produced by the application lag the field models.
Probe B's authority change is produced by a real peer campaigning over the in-process network, not by calling an internal transition.
No production logic is modified.

basis.prefix: Probe A initializes a voter through newRaft(newTestConfig(1,10,1,ms)) with ms holding entries 1..2 and HardState{Term:1,Commit:2}, then steps MsgHup, then a second identical node steps MsgTimeoutNow{From:3,Term:r.Term}, then raftLog.appliedTo(2,0) followed by MsgHup, plus a control node whose entry 2 is normal. Probe B elects a leader with MsgHup through newNetwork, commits one proposal, admits MsgReadIndex{Entries:[{Data:"A"}]} directly on the leader, then lets peer 2 campaign via the network, and finally admits MsgReadIndex{Data:"B"} on the new leader and steps one MsgHeartbeatResp carrying the context of the leader's own heartbeat.

scope.description: Same fixed harness as the previous execution with one added case. Probes A and B are unchanged (campaign admission with a committed-but-unapplied EntryConfChangeV2; ReadOnlySafe completion across a term change with its control). Probe C (TestAssuranceTransferWithLaggingTransferee) adds the bounded-liveness case for a requested leadership transfer: elect a 3-node leader over the in-process network, propose a ConfChangeV2 learner addition so followers hold a committed conf-change entry while their applied index lags, request TransferLeader to that lagging follower, and record leadTransferee, the transferee's state/term and hasUnappliedConfChanges, the error from a proposal issued while the transfer is pending, leadTransferee and proposal acceptance after the leader is ticked through its election timeout, and the outcome of a retry after the transferee's applied index reaches its committed index.
assumptions: Nodes come from the snapshot's own test constructors (newTestRaft/newTestConfig/newTestMemoryStorage/newNetwork) in one process; messages are delivered by the repository's own network helper.
The lagging applied index is produced by not advancing raftLog.applied for the transferee, which models an application that has not yet applied committed entries.
Ticks are the protocol's own logical time unit; the transfer is aborted by tickHeartbeat, not by a wall-clock timeout.
No production logic is modified.

basis.prefix: Probe C: newNetwork over newTestRaft(1,10,1,withPeers(1,2,3)) for ids 1..3; MsgHup on node 1 to elect; confChangeToMsg(ConfChangeV2{AddLearnerNode 4}) proposed via MsgProp on the leader and delivered by the network so both followers store the conf-change entry while their applied index stays behind; then MsgTransferLeader{From:2,Term:leader.Term} stepped into the leader; then MsgProp on the leader while leadTransferee != None; then electionTimeout tick() calls on the leader followed by another MsgProp; then raftLog.appliedTo(committed,0) on the transferee and a second MsgTransferLeader, which the network delivers and which lets the transferee campaign via MsgTimeoutNow.

scope.description: Fourth revision of the same fixed harness. Probes A, B and C are unchanged. Randomness is fixed per seed; absence of violations is a holds-only result for this event set, not a safety proof.

basis.prefix: For each of 60 seeds: build nodes 1..4 with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); nt := newNetwork(nodes[1],nodes[2],nodes[3]) then nt.peers[4] = nodes[4]. For 60 steps pick one of MsgHup on a random node, MsgProp with a tagged payload, tick() on a random node, isolate a random node, recover, TransferLeader from a random voter to the current leader, a ConfChangeV2 proposal on the leader (single change on node 4, half the time with Transition=JointImplicit), or persist/apply of all nodes; after each step persist/apply nodes 1..4 (applying committed conf changes through applyConfChange) and evaluate the four invariants, emitting a violation event with seed, step, nodes and operands when one is found, and finally emitting invariant_sweep_summary.
